title: WorkflowEntry schema rejects a document missing entityType, entityId, status, or changedBy
description: workflow-entry.model.js declares entityType, entityId, status, and changedBy as required fields with { timestamps: false }, and only changedAt defaults to Date.now. This unit test verifies Mongoose validation actually enforces those requirements at the model layer, independent of any controller-level checks, so a future code path can never silently persist an incomplete audit entry (e.g. one missing the actor).
preconditions: A test MongoDB instance (or mongodb-memory-server) with the WorkflowEntry model loaded
steps: Attempt WorkflowEntry.create({ entityId: <valid>, status: 'approved', changedBy: <valid user id> }) omitting entityType, and assert it throws a ValidationError.
Attempt WorkflowEntry.create({ entityType: 'evidence', status: 'approved', changedBy: <valid user id> }) omitting entityId, and assert it throws a ValidationError.
Attempt WorkflowEntry.create({ entityType: 'evidence', entityId: <valid>, changedBy: <valid user id> }) omitting status, and assert it throws a ValidationError.
Attempt WorkflowEntry.create({ entityType: 'evidence', entityId: <valid>, status: 'approved' }) omitting changedBy (the actor), and assert it throws a ValidationError.
Attempt a fully-populated WorkflowEntry.create(...) and assert it succeeds with changedAt auto-populated to the current time.
expectedResult: Each of steps 1-4 throws a Mongoose ValidationError and no document is persisted; step 5 succeeds and the saved document has a changedAt timestamp close to the test's execution time. This guarantees no evidence/mapping audit entry can ever be written without an identified actor, target, and resulting status, regardless of which controller code path calls WorkflowEntry.create.
